root_cause.text: Improper ordering of timer deletion and device reference cleanup during driver teardown allowed the inactivity_timer softirq to access freed backlight_device memory through two race windows: (1) put_device() before timer_delete_sync() enabled concurrent unbind to free the device while the timer softirq was still running, and (2) backlight cleanup before hid_hw_stop() allowed late HID event callbacks to re-arm the timer after deletion but before the final device reference was dropped.
root_cause.evidence: The patch reorders operations in both appletb_kbd_probe() error path and appletb_kbd_remove() to: (1) call hid_hw_close()/hid_hw_stop() before backlight cleanup to prevent new .event callbacks from reaching reset_inactivity_timer(), and (2) move timer_delete_sync() before put_device() within the backlight cleanup block to ensure the softirq is fully drained before the final reference is dropped. The KASAN trace shows the use-after-free occurs in appletb_inactivity_timer() calling backlight_device_set_brightness() -> mutex_lock() on freed memory, confirming the timer was executing after device deallocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource cleanup order in probe error path by stopping the inactivity timer before releasing the backlight device reference, and by deferring backlight cleanup until after hardware is fully stopped.
intent_record.what: Moved the backlight device cleanup block (if statement checking kbd->backlight_dev) from the 'close_hw' label to after the 'stop_hw' label, and reordered the operations within the block to call timer_delete_sync() before put_device().
intent_record.how: This changes the error handling cleanup sequence in the probe failure path. Previously, backlight cleanup occurred before hid_hw_close() and hid_hw_stop(). Now it occurs after both hardware operations complete. Additionally, the timer is deleted before the device reference is released, ensuring the timer is stopped before the device it may reference is freed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource cleanup ordering to prevent use-after-free by stopping hardware before backlight cleanup and deleting timer before releasing device reference.
intent_record.what: Reordered cleanup operations in appletb_kbd_remove(): moved hid_hw_close() and hid_hw_stop() calls before the backlight device cleanup block, and within that block swapped the order of timer_delete_sync() and put_device() calls.
intent_record.how: This change ensures hardware resources (HID device) are closed and stopped before cleaning up the backlight device and its associated timer. The timer is now deleted before the device reference is released, preventing potential use-after-free or resource leak scenarios where the timer might fire after the device is freed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code shows the vulnerable ordering in the error handling path. Line 442 calls put_device(&kbd->backlight_dev->dev) BEFORE line 445 calls hid_hw_stop(hdev). According to the vulnerability root cause, this ordering is incorrect because put_device() can free the backlight_device memory while the inactivity_timer softirq may still be running (the timer hasn't been deleted yet via timer_delete_sync()). The hid_hw_stop() at line 445 should be called BEFORE put_device() to ensure HID event callbacks are stopped before releasing the device reference. Additionally, there is no timer_delete_sync() visible in this snippet, which should be called before put_device() to prevent the timer softirq from accessing freed memory. The vulnerable construct is present: premature device reference cleanup (put_device) before proper hardware shutdown and timer deletion.

The vulnerable code (before the fix) had timer_delete_sync() called unconditionally in appletb_kbd_remove() and was missing it entirely in the error path of appletb_kbd_probe(). The fixed version (shown in the diff) now: (1) adds timer_delete_sync(&kbd->inactivity_timer) in the close_hw error path of appletb_kbd_probe() when kbd->backlight_dev exists, and (2) moves timer_delete_sync() to be conditional on kbd->backlight_dev in appletb_kbd_remove(), ensuring the timer is properly deleted before put_device() is called. The fix ensures the timer is deactivated before the device structure is freed, preventing the softirq from accessing freed memory.
